title: Flexible burst credits and invoice visibility for multi-plan customers
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers that subscribe to multiple plans or change plans mid-cycle report confusing invoices and unexpected overage charges when burst credits are applied at the tenant level. Current behavior lumps burst credit consumption into opaque quota adjustments and does not produce clear invoice line items when credits are consumed across multiple routes or plans.

This ticket defines requirements to: (1) decouple transient burst credits from long-term quota entitlements so credits are applied predictably per route or entitlement slice; (2) surface per-charge invoice visibility showing credit consumption, pro-rated plan changes mid-cycle, and per-route overage attributions; and (3) provide a rollback/appeal mechanism in the billing console for customers with disputed credit applications.
context: We already have per-plan quotas, per-route usage attribution, and soft-burst windows (see prior PRDs). However, invoices currently show a single overage line with a total token/embedding count and a lumpsum credit deduction which makes it hard for finance teams to reconcile. Several customers (Finance, Platform teams) requested improved transparency and a predictable way to apply burst credits when they own multiple plans or switch between Dedicated and Hosted during a billing period.
goals: Ensure burst credits are consumed in a deterministic order: per-route -> plan entitlements -> tenant-level credits
Expose invoice line items that break down: base plan charges, pro-rated plan changes, per-route usage, applied credits, and final overage charge
Support mid-cycle plan changes with pro-rated entitlements and automatic reconciliation visible in the console
Provide operator/CS tooling to adjust credit application and to issue invoice adjustments with audit trail
non_goals: Change pricing tiers or base per-token prices
Introduce real-time refunds; refunds will be processed as billing adjustments
Rework quota enforcement semantics outside burst-credit application order
requirements: API: Add /billing/preview endpoint that accepts a proposed plan change and a time window and returns a line-itemized cost preview
System: Burst credits must be tagged with scope (route_id, plan_id, tenant_id) and an application policy: first-match or proportional
Console: Invoice details page must show an expandable breakdown of credits applied with links to the usage traces that consumed each credit
Data: Billing ledger must store credit application events and the pro-rated entitlement computation for auditability
Migration: Run nightly backfill to annotate existing credits with best-effort scope (based on most-recent-route consumption) and include a flag for retroactive correction eligibility
acceptance_criteria: Given a tenant with two active plans, when a burst credit is issued scoped to tenant, the system applies credits first to the route-level usage that consumed the tokens, and the invoice shows which route consumed the credit

Given a mid-cycle upgrade from Plan A to Plan B, the billing preview API returns a line item showing pro-rated difference and projected applied credits; the resulting invoice reflects the pro-rated entitlement and credit usage
Invoices include explicit line items: base plan charges, pro-rated plan changes, per-route usage lines, credits applied (with credit ids), and final overage amount
The console invoice UI shows a link from each credit line to the usage slice (date range + route id) and to the backfilled ledger entry
Customer success can issue a billing adjustment in the console which creates an immutable audit record and updates the ledger; an API call to /billing/adjust returns 200 and a reference id
Nightly backfill completes for tenants with >1000 credits in staging and produces a backfill-report artifact in S3 for validation
edge_cases: Simultaneous plan switches in the same billing window across multiple sub-accounts: ensure deterministic ordering (old plan entitlement consumed first, then new plan)
Expired credits consumed after plan downgrade: credits must still apply if the consumption timestamp is within credit validity window
Zero-dollar invoices after credits: invoice must still be generated with line items and a zero total for accounting
success_metrics: Reduce customer billing disputes attributed to burst-credit confusion by 80% in Q2 post-release
Decrease CS time-to-resolution for credit disputes from median 3 business days to <1 business day
Increase % of invoices with full itemization available in console from 12% to 95% for multi-plan tenants
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): Implement API + ledger changes and run backfill on a snapshot of staging data; validate with finance team
Phase 2 (beta): Enable for selected enterprise customers behind feature flag; collect invoice samples and CS feedback
Phase 3 (general availability): Enable for all tenants and run live migration backfill in off-peak window with monitoring and rollback plan
qa_test_cases: Create tenant with two plans, generate route-specific usage that consumes a tenant-scoped burst credit, verify invoice line items and credit association
Simulate mid-cycle upgrade and run billing preview API; assert line items match expected pro-rata calculation
Backfill test: run migration on a snapshot and verify backfill-report contains mapping accuracy >95%
Adjustment test: CS issues a billing adjustment and observers confirm ledger and invoice are updated and audit trail exists
notes: Design: UI mockups in Confluence: https://confluence.company/billing/pm-66012-invoice-ui (see attachments)
Engineering: Kernel change required in billing-service to attach credit_id to consumption events; PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pulls/PR-1223
Finance: Reconciliation rules documented in Drive: https://drive.company.com/finance/billing-recon-2026
Consideration: For Dedicated customers with offline metering, we will accept upload batches and run a local reconciliation step before applying credits
Stakeholders: Finance (Maya Li), CS Escalations (Jordan Blake), Platform (Evelyn Chen)
Open question: Should tenant-level credits ever be forced to expire at billing boundary? Default is to keep validity window and surface expiration in invoice UI
